request_user:
Fact: eval_methodology
What to find: How evaluations were run (harness, settings, prompts, shots).
Card sections that often contain it: Evaluation, Methodology

Answer with status, value, quotes and section.

answer.value: Base models evaluated in an internal framework under the same settings, with few-shot counts per benchmark (e.g. 3–5-shot, 5-shot, 0-shot, 8-shot); scores within 0.3 considered equivalent. Instruct results use max reasoning effort (reasoning_effort=100) with temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95. Code agent benchmarks use the Minimal mode of DeepSeek Harness with a 1M-token context window (mini-SWE harness for DeepSWE v1.1, Claude Code harness for SEC-Bench Pro); visual agent benchmarks use the Claude Code harness with a 512k-token context window; Agent's Last Exam and AutomationBench use official scaffolds. Scaffold comparison uses N=8 samples per task on DeepSWE v1.1 and N=3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, Linux containers, 1M-token context limit, max_steps=500, Terminal-Bench 2.1 without network access.
quotes: All base models are evaluated in our internal framework under the same evaluation settings. Scores within 0.3 of each other are considered equivalent.
All instruct results below use the maximum effort setting (`reasoning_effort=100`). Evaluations use `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95`.
For code agent benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.1/3.0/4.0, DeepSWE v1.1, NL2Repo-Bench, ProgramBench), the model is evaluated with the Minimal mode of DeepSeek Harness and a 1M-token context window.
Visual agent benchmarks (Chartography, BabyVision, ZeroBench) use the Claude Code harness with a 512k-token context window.
All scaffolds use N=8 samples per task on DeepSWE v1.1 and N=3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, with Linux containers, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, a 1M-token context limit, and max_steps=500 per agent.
